subject: mathematics
question_text: Let a = i + 2j + 3k and b = 3i + j. Find a unit vector in the direction of a + b.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find a unit vector in the direction of a sum of two vectors.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Add and find the magnitude
steps.margin_note: First mark. Add first, THEN take the magnitude — |a+b| is not |a|+|b|. Note b has no k term, so the k component of the sum is just 3.

recall.must_convey: That a + b is found first as 4i + 3j + 3k, and its magnitude is √34.
accept: add them to get four i plus three j plus three k then the magnitude is root thirty four
first add the vectors then take the modulus
the sum is four i plus three j plus three k with magnitude root thirty four
modata add chesi tarvata magnitude teeskovali, root thirty four
add componentwise and find the length

steps.why: Adding vectors is componentwise, but magnitudes do not add — the length of a sum depends on the directions, which is why the addition must happen first.
common_mistakes: Adding the magnitudes of a and b separately.
Missing that b has a zero k component.

steps.label: Divide by the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Same finish as any unit-vector question: the sum over its own length.

recall.must_convey: That the unit vector is (a+b) divided by |a+b|, giving (4i+3j+3k)/√34.
accept: divide the sum by root thirty four
the unit vector is four i plus three j plus three k over root thirty four
a plus b over mod a plus b
sum ni magnitude tho divide cheyyali
answer is the sum divided by its length

steps.why: The direction of the answer is the direction of the SUM, not of a or b separately — which is what the question asked for.
common_mistakes: Dividing a and b separately and adding the results.
